pairs.why: A keeps the real slide's build: a tall green spiral around green posts, a thin blue ladder and a smooth finish, while B is a squat, chunky toy with a yellow column and water flowing down the chute.
A's large ball is tilted so the purple cap faces the viewer, as on the real card, while B is a smaller ball seen straight on, with the cap sitting on top.
A fills the frame with a smooth, softly glossy ball on finer sand, while B's tilt is closer to the real card but its grainy sand and smaller ball make it the more texture-heavy one.
A's three-quarter tilt, with the cap toward the viewer and green on top, matches the real ball's pose, while B is a flat front view.
A has gold rims and lugs on chrome stands with moderate shine, like the real kit, while B is chunkier and glossier, with gold-plated stands and feet that read as a toy statue.
These two are nearly identical, but A's thinner rims and quieter highlights sit slightly nearer the real kit's finish than B's thicker, shinier gold rims.
This pair is almost a tie, and A's slightly more restrained gloss and hardware match the real card a little better than B's chunkier rims.
A's chunky flower wreath, panelled door with wood grain and warm, rich light match the real door better, even though its extra lantern and flowerpot add clutter, while B is flatter and plainer.
